text:
maria: quick heads-up — after landing the fp8 mid-layer kernels change I'm seeing a regression on our 70-token chat benchmark when KV cache is enabled. p99 latency up ~24% on a single A100. :eyes:
bench-bot: auto-bench results uploaded: https://internal.ci/bench/1799004321 (summary attached)
jake: ugh. can you paste the microprofile output? curious if it's kernel selection thrashing or batching change
maria: here are the hot stacks from pprof for the 70-token run (kv on):
```
Top CPU:
  conv_kernel_dispatcher -> fp8_matmul -> quant_dequant -> kv_read -> generate_tokens
  p99 = 184ms (baseline 149ms)
```
lee: that stack smells like kernel selector flipping between fp8 and int8 for some layers at runtime. if selector can't decide stable kernel it can add overhead
sarah: also note calibration step changed — we now run per-batch recalib for layers marked "calib_sensitive" when kv is warm. might be triggering extra memcpy/convert ops
nathan: can we repro with kv disabled? that would isolate whether cache reads are interacting with FP8 path
maria: good call. kv disabled run is back to baseline. same model, same kernels, p99 ~150ms. so interaction point is kv+fp8
jake: do we have telemetry on kernel-choice churn per-request? adding a counter for selector mismatches would help
lee: ran a quick probe: selector used rule "latency_estimate" which uses samples from first 8 tokens. with kv warm we often start at token 9 path which invalidates the sample -> fallback decision runs and flips kernel. extra 2-3ms per flip but at scale adds up
sarah: I think the calibration code assumed cold-start prefix. when KV is hot, sequence offsets change the activation scale distribution. our per-layer calib table uses prefix-based stats which are now stale
maria: short-term mitigation: exclude encoder layers 4..10 from fp8 (keep int8) or disable per-request recalib when kv_enabled. both easy toggles in runtime config
nathan: can we try a targeted experiment: keep embedding and lm_head quant excluded (we already do that), plus force stable kernel choice by persisting selector decision per-model-version for 10s. that'll avoid churn for typical chat flows
jake: also measure batching heuristics — if batcher groups by "estimated kernel" we might be causing mixed-kernel microbatches; prefer grouping by kernel decision pre-dispatch
maria: here's the command I used to run benchmark locally:
```bash
./run_bench --model redwood-7b --seq-len 70 --kv-enabled --fp8-midlayers --concurrency 16 --profile pprof.out
```
bench-bot: micro-bench numbers (kv on):
  baseline(int8-all) p99=149ms, median=28ms
  fp8-midlayers p99=184ms, median=30ms
  fp8-midlayers + selector-cache p99=156ms, median=29ms
  fp8-midlayers + exclude-4-10 p99=151ms, median=28ms
lee: interesting — selector-cache gets most of the way there. that suggests overhead is mostly churn not raw kernel speed
sarah: longer-term fix: change calibration to accumulate stats keyed by (model-version, kv-offset-bucket) rather than prefix-only. then fp8 quant params will be correct regardless of cache warmup position
maria: filing an RFC/bug: 1799004321 — title: "FP8 mid-layer perf regression with KV warmup due to calibration & selector churn". I'll add perf traces and bench links
jake: can you add a short reproducer script and tag eng-ml + eng-runtime? I'll try the selector-cache patch tomorrow
maria: done. pushed repro + initial selector-cache PoC in branch fp8-selector-cache-1799. bench results in PR description
deploy-bot: deploy queued for canary cluster (fp8-selector-cache-1799) — run id: canary-1799005
nathan: for the bench plan: 1) baseline, 2) fp8-midlayers, 3) fp8+selector-cache, 4) fp8+exclude-range, 5) fp8+calib-bucket. run each x10 with kv on/off across A100 and T4
jake: also capture kernel pick histogram + memcopy counts. those are the likely overhead sources
maria: thanks all. I'll run the full matrix and post aggregated CSV later today. tagging @sarah for calibration design follow-up. :thumbsup:
